metadata.title: Use of Risk Assessment to Guide Decision-Making for Blood Pressure Management in the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology
top_takeaways: The updated 2025 AHA/ACC guidance recommends using the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equations instead of the Pooled Cohort Equations to estimate 10-year total cardiovascular disease risk (including ASCVD and heart failure) for guiding blood pressure treatment decisions.

A revised 10-year total cardiovascular disease risk threshold of ≥7.5% using the PREVENT equations is established to guide the initiation of antihypertensive pharmacological therapy in patients with stage 1 hypertension.

Comprehensive management of hypertension requires implementing risk assessment as the initial step through shared decision-making, facilitated by automated risk calculation in electronic health records and clinical decision support tools.

recommendations.statement: Estimate 10-year risk of total cardiovascular disease (including atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure) using the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations to guide decisions regarding the initiation of antihypertensive drug therapy in primary prevention.
recommendations.target_population: Adults being evaluated for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease and hypertension management
